title: Hold a steel plate down with one hand while the other slides a strong magnet off it, then pick up a nail with the magnet
instruction: Hold the steel plate down with one hand, and with the other slide the magnet off the plate's end by its knob and carry it well clear of the plate, without letting it snap back; then let go of the plate, pick up the steel nail on the table with the magnet and hold it up.
context: Strong pot and neodymium magnets are common in workshops and fabrication. They are taken off steel by sliding, not prying, and must be set down well clear: one that snaps back onto the steel crushes whatever is in between. A light plate slides along with the magnet, so it is held down while the magnet is slid off.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A loose grey steel plate, 770 g, 22 x 9 cm and 5 mm thick, lying along the left-right line 30 cm forward, from 4 cm right of the centre line to 18 cm left. (2) A loose neodymium pot magnet, 80 g: a red-painted steel cup 3.2 cm across and 8 mm tall, a steel stud 1.2 cm across and 3 cm tall and a black plastic knob 1.8 cm across on top. It clings to the plate (about 20 N) face down, 30 cm forward and 1 cm right of the centre line, 3 cm from the plate's right end. (3) A loose steel nail, 12 g, 8 cm long and 5 mm thick, lying on the table along the forward line, 30 cm forward and 17 cm right of the centre line. Brought within 1.8 cm of the magnet's face once the magnet is off the plate, the nail jumps onto the face and stays stuck there. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. Off: the magnet's rim at least 2 cm from the plate. Snapped back: once off, its rim came back within 4 mm of the plate, and then the trial scores 0. Picked up: the nail stuck on the magnet and at least 3 cm above the table. 1.0: the magnet's rim at least 5 cm from the plate and the nail picked up, never having snapped back, with the plate let go (both fingertip centres at least 3 cm from it) and the other arm (the one farther from the magnet) back where it started (its fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.5: off the plate at the end; 0.25: slid at least 2 cm along the plate at some point; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the magnet held still.
reset_notes: Put the magnet back face down on the plate, 3 cm from its right end, and lay the plate where it was.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the pull is a force the task file puts on the magnet (and back on the plate) each step: 20 N face on, times the share of its face over the plate (it fades off the edge); beside the plate 3 N / (1 + (gap / 8 mm)^3) toward it, the gap from the magnet's rim: 1 N at 1 cm, 0.18 N at 2 cm. The nail's pickup is a fixed joint the task file switches on. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
